extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students learning elementary combinatorics and proof techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions and solution-patterns for introductory combinatorics and elementary number-theory/proof exercises, showing standard counting techniques and proof styles (direct, contrapositive, cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Count sequences or choices by multiplying the number of options for each independent choice (e.g., for 5-character passwords over an alphabet of size k, |U| = k^5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly: compute |U| = 52^5 for upper+lower case letters; |A| = 9·10·10·5 for 4-digit even integers; for lists treat each position as a choice and multiply. Examples: passwords, lists, card lineups, binary strings beginning/ending with specified digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition Principle (sum over disjoint cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the set of outcomes splits into disjoint types, the total number is the sum of the counts of each type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: number of lists of form VV*** etc obtained by counting each form (720 each) and adding; number of flushes = sum of 5-card hands per suit. Often paired with the multiplication principle to count each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtraction Principle (complement counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count a property 'at least one' by computing total minus number with none (the complement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'at least one red card' = total lineups − lineups with no red cards; passwords with at least one uppercase = |U| − |X|. Also used to count 'have at least one repeated digit' by subtracting numbers with no repeats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion–Exclusion Formula
rubrics_metrics.description: For unions of sets use |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B| and for three sets the full inclusion–exclusion: |A ∪ B ∪ C| = sum singles − sum pairwise intersections + triple intersection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to count 4-card hands that are same suit or all red; to count binary strings satisfying several properties; explicit formula used |A ∪ B ∪ C| = |A|+|B|+|C|−|A∩B|−|A∩C|−|B∩C|+|A∩B∩C| with worked numeric example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pigeonhole Principle (division principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing n items into m boxes forces some box to contain at least ⌈n/m⌉ items; used to guarantee repeats or identical remainders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: choosing 6 integers gives two with same remainder mod 5; dice-rolling problem: to guarantee 10 or more of the same outcome with 6 faces one needs 55 rolls (ceil reasoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutations P(n,k) and Factorial Counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordered selections without replacement counted by P(n,k)=n·(n−1)·...·(n−k+1) and full permutations by n!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for lineups of cards P(52,7), permutations of letters where order matters (5! for arranging 5 symbols), counting arrangements with blocks (treat block as a single symbol then multiply by internal arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinations C(n,k) and Binomial Coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Unordered k-element subsets counted by C(n,k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!), used to choose positions or select subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: choose positions for 1's in binary strings; number of 10-digit integers with exactly three 6's by choosing three positions (C(10,3)) then filling remaining digits; many solutions rely on C(n,k) for position selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stars-and-Bars (multiset counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model placing identical items into distinct boxes as compositions counted by C(n+k−1,k−1) (or analogous formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to count multisets (10-element multisets from 4 symbols), placing 20 identical balls into 5 boxes, coin grabs (dollars in coins) and selection with identical copies. Examples show counting with and without a special element (white ball case) and with preselection adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary/string counting via choosing positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Count binary strings with specified number of 1's by choosing which positions are 1's: C(n,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: number of 16-digit binary strings with seven 1's is C(16,7); 8-digit strings ending in 1 or having exactly four 1's computed via position choices and inclusion–exclusion; ANB counts by fixing last bit then choosing remaining positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block/grouping method for permutations (treat consecutive items as a single symbol)
rubrics_metrics.description: When certain letters must appear consecutively, treat the block as one item and count permutations of the reduced set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: permutations of A,B,C,D,E,F,G in which ABC appear consecutively in that order: regard |ABC| plus other letters → 5! = 120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting by symmetry and pairing (complement pairing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use natural pairings (e.g., subset ↔ complement) to deduce parity or counts (e.g., C(2n,n) is even).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: each n-element subset of a 2n-element set pairs with its complement, so the total number of n-element subsets is even.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide into types/cases and count each (casework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Split complex constraints into exhaustive mutually exclusive types, count each with multiplication principle, then add.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: length-6 lists with two consecutive vowels divided into five possible positions for the VV block, each counted similarly (720 each), then summed to 3600. Other examples partition by whether last digit is 0 or not when counting numbers with three zeros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stars-and-bars with constraints (capacity or 'at most one' constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: When boxes have capacity constraints, map to appropriate model (e.g., at most one per box → choose positions → C(n,k)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: placing 15 identical balls into 20 boxes with at most one per box corresponds to choosing 15 boxes from 20, C(20,15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Binomial Theorem for identities and coefficient extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (x+y)^n expansion to compute coefficients, derive identities like sum of binomial coefficients = 2^n and alternating sums = 0, or coefficient extraction by plugging y=2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: find coefficient of x^8 in (x+2)^13 by binomial theorem; show sum_{k} C(k,?) identities by substituting values into (1+1)^n etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double counting / combinatorial proof technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Count the same set in two different ways to derive an identity (e.g., choose committee then leaders vs choose leaders then fill out committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: C(n,k)·C(k,2) = C(n,2)·C(n−2,k−2) derived by two approaches to selecting a committee and two leaders; used to prove combinatorial equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting by choosing the largest (or distinguished) element
rubrics_metrics.description: Count k-element subsets by fixing the largest element and summing counts for each possible largest value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to prove identity sum_{k=m}^{n} C(k,m) = C(n+1,m+1): fix largest element k and count choices for remaining m elements from the k elements to its left.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutations of multisets (multinomial / repeated-item formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count permutations of a word with repeated letters by n! divided by product of factorials of multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'TENNESSEE' permutations computed by Fact 3.8; counting numbers with repeated digits by computing permutations of multiset of digits (e.g., three 3's, one 4, one 8 → 5!/(3!1!1!) = 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive blanks-and-positions counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Model sequences as blank positions and build by selecting positions for special entries then filling remaining blanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurring motif: start with blank list of length n, choose slots for chosen digits/letters (C(n,k)), then fill other slots with available options (multiplication principle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity/proof-by-cases using representations 2a or 2a+1
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove even/odd statements, express even integers as 2a and odd as 2a+1 and perform algebraic manipulations; handle cases separately when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: proofs that x^2 even implies x even (contrapositive), sums/products parity proofs, showing n^2+3n+4 even for any integer n by separate parity cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof by Contrapositive and Proof by Cases (explicit proof styles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use contrapositive to prove implications and split into exhaustive cases when direct approach is cumbersome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many number-theory exercises use 'Proof. (Contrapositive)' or 'We consider two cases' templates; examples include: if n^2 even then n even (contrapositive) and several parity/divisibility proofs by cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular arithmetic congruence properties
rubrics_metrics.description: If a ≡ b (mod n) then expressions built from a and b preserve congruence (e.g., a^2 ≡ b^2 (mod n), a^k ≡ b^k (mod n)); proofs via factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: proofs that a ≡ b (mod n) implies a^2 ≡ b^2 (mod n) and a^2 ≡ ab (mod n) by showing n divides differences via factoring (a^2−b^2)=(a−b)(a+b) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisibility arguments via factorization and prime-factor considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Show divisibility by factoring or by analyzing prime factors; use that factorials contain primes and that primes do not appear in smaller factorials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: showing p divides C(p,k) for 0

rubrics_metrics.name: Vandermonde's convolution / sum of product of binomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity: sum_{k} C(m,k) C(n,p−k) = C(m+n,p), counting p-element subsets of A∪B by choosing k from A and p−k from B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit combinatorial proof presented: split S=A∪B and count p-element subsets by summing over possible k chosen from A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting lists with exact counts of symbols via multinomial/permutation arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute number of sequences with specified multiplicities by multinomial coefficients: n!/(n1! n2! ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: number of permutations for sequences with specified counts of digits/letters (e.g., two 3's two 4's one 8 counted as permutations of multiset).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of complement and length-type splitting in decimal-digit enumeration
rubrics_metrics.description: When counting integers within a range (like 1 to 9999) split by number of digits (1-,2-,3-,4-digit cases), count each separately respecting leading-zero constraints and sum (or take complement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: count integers 1..9999 with no repeated digits by considering 1-,2-,3-,4-digit numbers separately using first-digit nonzero constraints and multiplication principle, then sum.
